class S2D4P.data.dataset.dataset_abc.AddedTimeFeatures(reference_config: DatasetConfigABC, time_features: list[str] | None = None)

Bases: object

Generate temporal features for dataset samples.

Requested initialization-time, lead-time, month, and day-of-year features are computed from sample coordinates. Linear time features are normalized against the dataset temporal extent, while periodic calendar features use sine and cosine encodings.

Parameters:

  • reference_config (DatasetConfigABC) – Dataset configuration providing temporal coverage, lead times, and dimension names used to construct temporal features.

  • time_features (list[str] | None) – Temporal features to generate. Supported values are the initialization- time dimension, lead-time dimension, "month_sin", "month_cos", "day_sin", and "day_cos".

build_time_features(sample_coords: dict[str, ndarray]) → AddedTimeFeatures

Build temporal features for all dataset samples.

Target times are calculated from initialization and lead times. Requested linear temporal features are normalized, while month and day-of-year features are represented using cyclic sine and cosine encodings.

Parameters:

sample_coords (dict[str, np.ndarray]) – Sample coordinates containing initialization and lead times for each dataset sample.

Returns:

This instance with time_features_array populated for all samples.

Return type:

AddedTimeFeatures

Raises:

ValueError – If required sample coordinates are missing, the reference temporal span has zero length, or lead time normalization would use a zero maximum.

reference_config: DatasetConfigABC
time_features: list[str] | None = None

class S2D4P.data.dataset.dataset_abc.DatasetConfigABC

Bases: ABC

Abstract base class for configuring pipeline datasets.

Defines the shared interface for selecting forecast and conditioning data, resolving conditioning methods, validating compatibility between data sources, and selecting forecast lead times. Train and Inference datasets inherit from this class to implement specific data-loading.

Supports ensemble-mean, cross-ensemble, same-member, and static conditioning. Forecast data can also serve as the conditioning source when a separate conditioning dataset is not provided.

Subclasses must implement available_times, ds_operator, effective_input, and build_dataset. The following attributes must be defined in subclasses including both Train and Inference pipelines:

forecast

Configuration for the forecast data. Could only be None for Inference pipeline where the conditioning dataset must provide the required input.

Type:

ForecastDataConfig | None

condition

Optional configuration for auxiliary conditioning data. If None, forecast data may be reused as conditioning data, depending on the selected conditioning method.

Type:

ConditionDataConfig | None

condition_method

Method used to associate conditioning data with forecast inputs. Supported methods are “ensemble_mean”, “cross_ensemble”, “same_member”, and “static”.

Type:

str | None

lead_times

Requested forecast lead times. Accepts a lead-time configuration or an explicit sequence. If None, all available input lead times are selected.

Type:

lead_time_config | list | np.ndarray | None

abstract property available_times

Return the time span available for dataset construction. This is different than input time because it should be the common time range resolved by the forecast and if available, the reference data. Forecasts range is based on initialization time and lead time, while reference data has one time resolution.

For instance, for decadal predictions, the initial times are the start of the years, but the available times are the span of coverage based on initial_time / lead_time span which has a monthly resolution.

Subclasses must implement this property to determine which initialization times satisfy their input and target data requirements.

abstract build_dataset()

Construct the dataset from this validated configuration.

Subclasses must implement this method to assemble the required forecast, conditioning, and optional reference data according to their dataset-specific sampling and preprocessing procedures.

condition: ConditionDataConfig | None
condition_method: str | None
abstract property ds_operator

Return the dataset-specific operator.

Subclasses must implement this property to provide the operator used for their dataset construction and data access.

Recommended implementaion is from S2D4P.data_modules.dataset.operator import DatasetOperator.

property effective_condition: ConditionDataConfig | ForecastDataConfig | None

final get_input_times(requested_times: Sequence[datetime64 | datetime | datetime] | ndarray | DataArray)

Resolve requested initialization times against the effective input.

Validates that all requested times are available to the dataset, and selects those present in the effective input’s initialization-time coordinates to iterate over.

The intention for this code is the dataset available temporal coverage is based on the forecast/condition/reference common time span. But, the exact initial times to be iterated over is not necessarily the same as the available times. See documentation for available_times for more details.

Parameters:

requested_times (Sequence[np.datetime64 | datetime.datetime | cftime.datetime] | np.ndarray | xr.DataArray) – Requested initialization times. Non-xarray inputs are converted to a DataArray indexed by the initialization-time dimension.

Returns:

Requested initialization times that are present in the effective input dataset, preserving their original order.

Return type:

xr.DataArray

Raises:

ValueError – If any requested initialization time is not included in available_times.

class S2D4P.data.dataset.dataset_abc.lead_time_config(list_lead_times: list | None = None, start: int = 1, end: int | None = None)

Bases: object

Configuration for selecting forecast lead times.

Supports either an explicit list of lead times or an inclusive range defined by starting and ending lead times. Lead times are one-based.

Parameters:

  • list_lead_times (list | None, default None) – Explicit list of lead times to select. If provided, start and end are ignored.

  • start (int, default 1) – First lead time in the selected range. Used only when list_lead_times is None.

  • end (int | None, default None) – Last lead time in the selected range, inclusive. Required when list_lead_times is None.

build_lead_times()

Construct the selected forecast lead times.

Returns the explicitly specified lead times, if available. Otherwise, generates an inclusive sequence from start to end.

Returns:

Selected lead times. Returns the original list when list_lead_times is provided.

Return type:

list | np.ndarray

class S2D4P.data.dataset.operator.DatasetOperator(config: DatasetConfigABC)

Bases: object

Coordinate dataset-level preprocessing, weighting, and metadata operations.

Provides shared operations across forecast, reference, and conditioning data configured by a dataset configuration.

Parameters:

config (DatasetConfigABC) – Dataset configuration defining the active data sources and preprocessing pipelines.

Add a fitted preprocessing module to all active pipelines.

Parameters:

  • preprocessor (PreprocessModuleABC) – Fitted preprocessing module to add.

  • index (int) – Position at which the preprocessing module is inserted.

Raises:

  • TypeError – If preprocessor is not an instance of PreprocessModuleABC.

  • ValueError – If preprocessor has not been fitted.

property config_reference

Return the configured reference dataset when available.

Returns:

Reference data configuration, or None when the dataset configuration does not define reference data.

Return type:

DataConfigABC | None

fit_preprocessors(train_times: Sequence[datetime64 | datetime | datetime] | ndarray | DataArray, save=False, save_path: Path | str | None = None, save_name: str | None = None)

Fit active preprocessing pipelines using training data.

Training times are validated against the available dataset times before forecast, reference, and conditioning preprocessing pipelines are fitted. Temporal training masks are applied to forecast and non-static conditioning data.

Parameters:

  • train_times (Sequence[np.datetime64 | datetime.datetime | cftime.datetime] | np.ndarray | xr.DataArray) – Initialization times used to fit preprocessing statistics.

  • save (bool) – Whether fitted preprocessing pipelines are saved.

  • save_path (Path | str | None) – Directory in which fitted preprocessing pipelines are saved.

  • save_name (str | None) – Optional filename used when saving preprocessing pipelines.

Raises:

ValueError – If one or more requested training times are unavailable.

get_weights(config: WeightsConfig | None = None, save: bool = True, save_path: Path | str | None = None, save_name: str | None = None) → DataArray

Build loss weights from the configured target data.

Reference data are used when available; otherwise, forecast data define the target coordinates and variables. If the target preprocessing pipeline contains a flattener, it is supplied when constructing the weights.

Parameters:

  • config (WeightsConfig | None) – Configuration used to construct loss weights. If None, default weight settings are used.

  • save (bool) – Whether generated weights are saved.

  • save_path (Path | str | None) – Directory in which generated weights are saved.

  • save_name (str | None) – Optional filename used when saving generated weights.

Returns:

Generated loss weights aligned with target dimensions and variables.

Return type:

xr.DataArray

Raises:

  • RuntimeError – If channel-specific weights do not match the configured output variables.

  • ValueError – If neither reference nor forecast data are available to define the target coordinates.
